title: Bilinear block mechanism

new_result.scope: Literal original-coordinate disjoint L,R with |L|=3, |R|=2; rank A[L,R]=2; if w is the cross product of the two physical cross columns and A[L,L]w is nonzero, arbitrary same-side curvature on both banks, arbitrary conditioned outside couplings/curvature, arbitrary affine terms and arbitrary signs are retained.
new_result.bound: ||p_Q||_infinity <= [5*6^(3/5)/2^(11/10)] (||w|| ||P w||)^(-1/5), constant 6.834830666196632; same coefficient times interval length; phi_Q in L1 so branch density is continuous.
new_result.mechanism: Quadratic-fiber coarea + Hausdorff-Young gives an L4 time budget. The phase derivative is exactly 2(Pn)^T Y+beta, a genuine original-product linear projection, so its inverse-half moment is controlled without a conditional density supremum. Two-dimensional bilinear Plancherel gives |phi(t)|<=pi |t|^-1 A(t), integrated before inversion. No probability squaring or post-rotation independence.
new_result.target_application: Q_tau=2Y1Y3+tau Y3^2+2Y1Z1+2Y2Z2 has at least four eigenvalues of modulus >=1 for every real tau and satisfies ||p||_infinity <=6.8348306662(1+tau^2)^(-1/10).

pinned_result_applied.application: F_m=2X0<c,Y>+<v1,Y>^2+<v2,Y>^2 with flat orthonormal Walsh c,v1,v2, m>=8. Mixed Gram I3, leverage 3/m<=1/2, active spectrum {-1,1,1,1}. Gives |phi(t)|<=8pi^2|t|^-2 and ||p||_infinity<=4sqrt(2), with linear interval bound.

partner_result_applied.application: At tau=0 in Q_tau, Delta=1 and shear norm=1, giving ||p||_infinity<=5.950065686491101. The new theorem extends uniformly to all tau.

obstruction.statement: For even m, take fixed left shear P e3=e1 and right cross columns sqrt(2/m)e1 on half the coordinates and sqrt(2/m)e2 on the other half. The active spectrum is {sqrt(2),1,-1,-sqrt(2)} plus zeros. The fixed-triple V1 packet sum equals 1, but every individual currency ||w||||Pw||=4/m^2 tends to zero. Therefore aggregate V1 cannot be closed by choosing one physical pair. This is not a QFORM counterexample.

first_unpaid_implication: QFORM-V1-AGGREGATE-KERNELDERIVATIVE-v1: convert a universal amount of V1 overlap mass into an aggregate source-coordinate kernel-derivative/crossing estimate before reciprocal packet selection, or route the diffuse packet law into an already-paid grouped-cross exit; then handle any remaining higher-overlap strata.
